reason: The contract (problem.txt, the operative artifact contract; no test.py/get_inputs exist) requires abs(actual[i] - atan(x[i])) <= 1e-6 for EVERY finite FP16 value, with rel tol zero, correctness being a single verdict over the entire legal domain. An exhaustive sweep of all 63488 finite FP16 bit patterns through the actual kernel (probe t8) shows max absolute error 5.03e-6 vs FP64 atan, with 5606 values violating the 1e-6 tolerance (worst at 0.6220703125) — this is a direct, in-scope violation of the explicitly required numeric tolerance, not a rounding/representation artifact the contract accounts for. Probe t9 further confirms a discontinuous error spike across the 0.66 branch boundary (~5.8e-7 below vs ~4.9e-6 above) and violations near the 2.414213562373095 boundary. Both claims (c1, c2) are confirmed, in_scope, and tied by scope evidence to the stated input domain (every finite FP16 value). Skeptic reviewed the evidence and recorded no new claims. The kernel's truncated 4–5 digit rational-coefficient approximation simply cannot meet the 1e-6 absolute tolerance the contract mandates.
